# Testing on both engines

Every store and core test runs on SQLite, and on Postgres as well when `DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set ([plan invariant 3](plan.md#invariants)). Tests always run with the race detector.

## Running

```sh
make test       # every test, SQLite only; Postgres tests skip
make test-pg    # every test on SQLite and Postgres
make check      # generated code up to date, go vet, then both of the above
DARKORY_TEST_S3=1 DARKORY_TEST_SMTP=1 make test   # also MinIO and Mailpit in Docker
make web-check  # the web app: typecheck, eslint, vitest (needs node; run `npm ci` in web/ first)
make e2e        # the real binary end to end, the bots and the soak, on SQLite (about 3 minutes)
make e2e-pg     # the same on Postgres, plus two server processes on one database (about 6 minutes)
cd web && npm run e2e   # build the web app and the binary, then drive a real server in Chromium (needs node and go; `npx playwright install chromium` once)
```

The end-to-end suite in `e2e/` runs only with `DARKORY_E2E=1`, so `make check` skips it. It builds `darkory` once into a temporary directory, runs `darkory init` and `darkory serve` processes on free ports, and drives them through the CLI, `darkory mcp` over stdio and, for the soak, the generated client; it imports nothing under `internal/`. With `DARKORY_E2E_POSTGRES_URL` set (as `make e2e-pg` does) each test creates its own `dk_e2e_<random>` database and drops it. `DARKORY_E2E_SOAK=5m` makes the soak longer, `DARKORY_E2E_SOAK_TASKS=3000` heavier, and `DARKORY_E2E_RACE=1` builds the binary with the race detector, whose reports fail the run through the server log check.

`make test-pg` sets `DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://dk@localhost:54329/postgres?sslmode=disable`. Point it elsewhere with `make test-pg TEST_POSTGRES_URL=…`, or set the variable yourself for a single package:

```sh
DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL='postgres://dk@localhost:54329/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test -race ./internal/store/...
```

## Bots

`tools/bots/bot` is a library of bots: agent Members that work an Install as an agent such as Claude Code does — `next`, a Heartbeat in the background, a Note, Evidence, a question, a Handover or a Complete — through the generated client, and, for `stuck`, through the real binary; and human personas that act as people in the web app would, each with a token of their own. Like `e2e/`, it imports nothing under `internal/`. The bots work a **preset**: a Go value (`bot.Preset`) holding the Teams with their defaults, the Skills, the Statuses, the Workspaces (each made as a throwaway git repository), the agents, the personas and the Feature templates, with the Tasks the planner files for each (title, one-line description, Skill, Workspaces, Backlog or not, Blocking, the question its worker raises and at whom, the Skill it is handed over to, the workpaper its worker appends to, what review hands back). `bot.Setup` makes a preset idempotently by name; `e2e/bots_test.go` (`TestBots`, the software preset) and `e2e/bots_accounting_test.go` (`TestBotsAccounting`), both part of `make e2e` and `make e2e-pg`, run the bots at the `fast` pace as scenario tests; `tools/bots` runs them at the `human` pace as a live load, so the web app can be watched and screenshotted with work going on.

### The software preset

Teams `WEB` and `OPS`; Skills `build`, `build-acme` (company), `review`, `qa`, `docs`, `triage`, `deploy`; the Organisation's own Statuses (the preset sets none) and no Workspace. The planner files `DefaultPlan`, whose Task descriptions carry the worker's directions as lines (`Question for <member>: …`, `Hand over to review when built.`), which any Task filed by hand may carry too.

| Who | Skills | What it does | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planner` | breakdown | Takes Break downs through `next` and files the Feature's Tasks: two builds into Todo; review and QA into the Backlog, blocked by both builds, then moved to Todo; a help page, a demo and a polish into the Backlog. Completes the Break down with a Note. | Filing into a backlog Status and Blocking before anything is takeable. |
| `builder-1`, `builder-2` | build, build-acme, qa | `next` with a model label, Heartbeats in the background, a Note, a small Evidence file. A question in the description is filed aimed at its Member, blocking the Task, and the builder waits holding its Claim (releasing it after `Patience`). `Hand over to review when built.` hands over to `review` and In review; anything else completes with an Observation, didn't work when it had to ask. | Questions, Handover into a named Status, Observations. |
| `reviewer` | review, skill-review | Completes a review with a Note; completes a Retrospective with a pending proposal, publishing it, or hands it back to `retro` when another version was published since. | Publishing a Skill version, the stale base. |
| `retro` | retro | Reads the Feature's Observations, proposes the next version of the company Skill that didn't work (`build-acme`), and hands over to `skill-review`. | The Retrospective's proposal. |
| `lapser` | triage | Claims with a 2 s timeout (20 s at the human pace) and never heartbeats. Once in the test; every minute live. | The lapse recorded with no actor; the Task back in Todo. |
| `stuck` | deploy | `darkory next`, then `darkory heartbeat run` keeping the Claim and `darkory heartbeat <task>` checking it until someone takes the Task back, when that command exits 3. | Take-back through the CLI; `heartbeat run` keeps the Session's other Claims (decisions.md). |
| `prober` | docs | A builder that asks `next` without waiting. | `next` offers nothing waiting in the Backlog until a person moves it. |
| `kai` (persona) | — | Owns the Features; every round ships those whose Tasks have all ended and moves one unblocked Backlog Task of a Feature whose Break down has ended to Todo; the agents report to him. | Ship, the owner's Status move. |
| `mai` (persona) | — | Answers the questions aimed at her: Claim, a Note with the answer, Complete. | A question ends and its Task unblocks. |

`TestBots` sets the Organisation up with the bots' own `bot.Setup`, twice (the second must change nothing but the tokens), runs the agents but not the personas, and acts itself as ada (admin), kai (owns the Feature, and the agents report to kai) and mai (answers the question). It checks each scenario as it happens — the stuck Claim In progress in `GET /v1/tasks` with its holder and a moving expiry, the lapse back to Todo with no actor, kai's take-back and stuck's exit 3, the prober offered nothing until mai moves the help page and then exactly it, a watcher never seeing a holder on a Backlog Task, the question blocking a Task mai alone can take, the Handover landing In review, ship refused then shipped once kai drops the Backlog leftovers, `build-acme` v2 published by the reviewer — and then, with the bots stopped, every Task's Status against the soak's rule and a replay of the whole Activity, and the order of the trail (gapless, each Claim ended once before the next, the question filed and blocking in one write inside the builder's one Claim, the Retrospective filed in the ship's write, the version published in the review's). It takes about 15 s on either engine.

### The accounting preset

Teams `BOOK` Bookkeeping (ship when done by default) and `TAX` Tax, both working in the Workspace `clients`: a git repository of client folders, `<client>/<period>/`, with plain-text workpapers (`documents.txt`, `bank-reconciliation.txt`, `bas-worksheet.txt`, `lodgement.txt` and so on) that the bots append a dated line to, commit, and attach as Evidence. Skills, written as the firm's procedures: `bookkeeping`, `reconciliation` (company, on bookkeeping), `tax-review`, `lodgement`, `client-comms`, `review` and the built-ins. Statuses: Awaiting client (backlog: not takeable until the client's documents arrive), Todo, In progress, In review, Lodged (done), Dropped. Features: "Q1 BAS — Northwind Traders" (ship when done), "FY26 accounts — Contoso Pty Ltd", the quick "Fix the GST code on invoice 1042" and "Q1 BAS — Fabrikam Cafe"; every Feature has a description and every Task a one-line one, and the Steps, not the descriptions, carry what a worker does.

| Who | Skills | What it does | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planner` | breakdown | Files each Feature's Tasks from its template: Collect into Todo, Reconcile and the asset register into Awaiting client, the rest blocked in a chain (Collect → Reconcile → Draft → Lodge) and moved to Todo once blocked. | Templates; a backlog Status with another name. |
| `drafter` | bookkeeping, reconciliation, client-comms | Collects, reconciles and drafts: appends the Step's line to its workpaper in the Task's Workspace, commits it and attaches the file. Collecting Q1 BAS, asks Mai "Statements for March are missing — ask Northwind?", blocking Collect while it holds it; on Contoso's bank reconciliation asks about a $4,200 transfer. Hands the drafts over to `tax-review` and the quick fix to `review`, In review; after a hand-back appends the fix and hands over again. | Workspaces on Tasks, Evidence from a repository, questions, Handover. |
| `reviewer-tax` | tax-review, review, skill-review | Completes a review; hands Contoso's financial statements back to bookkeeping, in Todo, the first time ("Depreciation on the van is missing…"); publishes Retrospectives' proposals. | Hand-back; the quick Feature shipping on its review. |
| `retro` | retro | As in the software preset; Contoso's question makes it propose `reconciliation` v2. | A company Skill improved by a Retrospective. |
| Mai Tran (persona, client manager) | client-comms, lodgement | Answers the questions aimed at her 20–60 s after they are asked (Claim, Note, Complete), and lodges: takes lodgement Tasks, appends the receipt to the lodgement workpaper, attaches it and completes. | A question lands with its Member; ship-when-done fires on her completion. |
| Kai Nguyen (persona, partner) | — | Owns the Features; every 30 s ships those whose Tasks have all ended (FY26; the BAS and the quick fix ship themselves) and moves one unblocked Task waiting in Awaiting client, of a Feature whose Break down has ended, to Todo. The agents report to him. | Awaiting client is never offered until moved; owner's ship. |

`TestBotsAccounting` runs every bot and persona of the preset on a fresh Install (`init --no-agents`), Setup twice, and the admin files Q1 BAS, the quick fix and FY26 for Kai. It holds Kai back until Reconcile (its blocker ended) and the asset register have sat in Awaiting client untaken and not takeable by the drafter, then checks that each is taken only after Kai's move; that the question is aimed at Mai, blocks Collect in the same write inside the drafter's one Claim, is claimed by Mai alone, and that Collect completes after her answer and before Reconcile's move; that Draft the BAS lands In review and reviewer-tax completes it; that the quick Feature ships in its review's completion with no Retrospective and Q1 BAS in Mai's completion of Lodge, filing its Retrospective; and, with the bots stopped and their tokens revoked, every Status against its Claims and a replay of the Activity, the workpapers committed in the repository, the Evidence small text, every Note one sentence. It takes about 6 s on SQLite and 11 s on Postgres.

### The live load

`go run ./tools/bots` takes an admin's token and a preset, makes what the preset needs when it is missing (Teams, Skills, Statuses, Workspaces with their repositories, the agents reporting to the manager persona, the personas in their Teams with their Skills, the admin in every Team; names are kept, a deactivated Member is reactivated), issues each bot and persona a fresh token named `tools/bots <time>`, files the preset's Features in turn, owned by the manager persona, when fewer than `--features` have work left (and, for software, a Chores Feature in `OPS` for the lapser and stuck), builds `./cmd/darkory` when the preset has stuck, and prints every step as it happens, starting with the preset. When it stops — after `--for` (10 minutes by default; `0` runs until Ctrl-C) or on Ctrl-C — it revokes the tokens it issued, which ends any Claim a bot or persona still holds.

It needs an Install with Statuses (migration 0003) and, for Workspaces, migration 0004. Against `make dev`'s Install (the server on 7358; use 7357 with `make serve`), from the repository root of the checkout `make dev` runs in, in a second terminal:

```sh
DARKORY_TOKEN=$(grep -o 'dk_[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' .dev/init.txt | head -1) \
  go run ./tools/bots --url http://127.0.0.1:7358 --preset accounting --pace human --for 10m
```

```
14:02:00.112 preset accounting on http://127.0.0.1:7358 as tuongaz: planner, drafter, reviewer-tax, retro in BOOK and TAX, reporting to Kai Nguyen, asking Mai Tran; Mai Tran and Kai Nguyen; Features owned by Kai Nguyen; pace human, for 10m0s
14:02:00.112 Workspace clients is the git repository /Users/you/src/darkory/.dev/bots/clients
14:02:00.118 owner filed BOOK-1 "Q1 BAS — Northwind Traders" for Kai Nguyen; the planner will break it down
14:02:00.124 owner filed BOOK-3 "Fix the GST code on invoice 1042" for Kai Nguyen, a quick Feature with its one Task BOOK-4
14:03:41.502 drafter    asked        BOOK-5 BOOK-9 aimed at Mai Tran: "Statements for March are missing — ask Northwind?"; BOOK-5 is blocked until it ends
14:04:23.870 Mai Tran   noted        BOOK-9 "Northwind sent the March statements this morning; they are in the folder now."
14:05:00.341 Kai Nguyen moved        BOOK-6 "Reconcile bank feed" from Awaiting client to Todo
14:05:52.016 drafter    wrote        BOOK-6 "At 31 March 2026 the statement balance of $48,213.07 agrees to the ledger, with 214 lines matched and none unreconciled." to northwind-traders/2026-q1/bank-reconciliation.txt in clients
14:07:10.655 drafter    handed over  BOOK-7 to tax-review, now In review, with the Note "The workpaper bas-worksheet.txt is attached and ready for tax-review."
14:09:31.204 reviewer-tax handed back  TAX-7 to bookkeeping: "Depreciation on the van is missing from the profit and loss; add it and send it back."
```

At the human pace a worker spends 30–90 s on a Task and heartbeats every 15 s (Claims time out after 45 s), a persona answers or lodges 20–60 s after a Task becomes theirs, the owner persona looks over their Features every 30 s, the lapser lapses once a minute, stuck holds its Task until someone takes it back and takes it again two minutes later, and a worker waits three minutes for an answer before releasing its Task. What a person can do while it runs: answer a question from the Inbox, with `--humans=false` (it is then aimed at the admin, or at `--ask`); drag a Task from the Backlog (Awaiting client) to Todo and watch it taken; take back stuck's "Deploy to staging"; watch a hand-back and the rework; ship a Feature, after which retro proposes the company Skill's next version and the reviewer publishes it. `--humans=false` runs as before personas existed: the admin owns the Features, the questions are aimed at the admin, and `--ship` ships the admin's Features as they end, dropping what waited in the Backlog a round after the rest ended. `--pace fast` runs everything at the tests' pace. Never point it at an Install whose record matters: it files Features and Tasks under the admin's name and, for accounting, replaces the Statuses (renaming Backlog to Awaiting client and Done to Lodged, keeping their ids). Both presets can run on one Install one after the other (the software bots read the Statuses by kind), but not at once: they share the agents `planner` and `retro` by name, and a planner breaks down whatever Feature its Teams hold with its own preset's plans.

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--url` | `DARKORY_URL`, else `http://127.0.0.1:7357` | the Install |
| `--token` | `DARKORY_TOKEN` | an admin's token (the variable keeps it out of `ps`) |
| `--preset` | `software` | `software` or `accounting` |
| `--humans` | on | run the preset's personas, each with its own token; off, the admin is asked and owns the Features |
| `--workspace-root` | `bots` in `DARKORY_DATA`, else `.dev/bots` | where a preset's Workspaces get their repositories, `<root>/<name>`; a Workspace that exists keeps its path |
| `--pace` | `human` | `human` or `fast` |
| `--for` | `10m` | how long the bots work; `0` until interrupted |
| `--team`, `--team-name`, `--ops`, `--ops-name` | the preset's (`WEB` Web, `OPS` Ops; `BOOK` Bookkeeping, `TAX` Tax) | rename the preset's first and second Team |
| `--ask` | the answering persona, else the admin | who the agents' questions are aimed at, unless a Step names someone |
| `--features` | `3` | Features with work left to keep filed |
| `--ship` | off | ship the admin's Features as they end (with `--humans=false`) |
| `--darkory` | built from `./cmd/darkory` | the binary stuck runs |
| `--insecure` | off | let stuck's CLI use plain `http://` to another host |

## Runner

The Runner (`internal/runner`, [ADR 0013](../adr/0013-a-runner-starts-agent-sessions.md)) pulls Tasks through `next` as each agent Member it has a token for, prepares a git worktree per Workspace the Task names under `<data>/workspaces/<KEY>/`, writes `<data>/sessions/<KEY>/prompt.md` and `mcp.json`, starts the agent's command — in tmux when the machine has it, as a child process otherwise, logging to `pane.log` — sends Heartbeats while the session's progress file moves, nudges an agent that stops without a decision, ends the session when the Claim ends and attaches the log as Evidence. It merges a Task's branch into `feature/<FEATURE-KEY>` when its review completes, and that into the default branch at Ship ([ADR 0014](../adr/0014-feature-branches-and-shipping.md)).

```sh
darkory serve --data .dev                 # runs the Runner too when .dev/agents holds <member>.token files (--runner=auto)
darkory serve --data .dev --runner=off    # the server alone; then, in another terminal:
DARKORY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7357 darkory runner --data .dev [--member builder]…
darkory sessions                          # what the Runner runs now ("No Runner is attached" when serve has none)
darkory join WEB-12 [--readonly] [--data .dev]     # join the session's tmux pane; detach with the prefix and d
darkory sessions nudge WEB-12 | darkory sessions stop WEB-12   # admins
```

The sessions run on a tmux server of the Runner's own, `tmux -L darkory-<8 hex of the data directory's path>`, so `tmux ls` does not show them; `darkory join` finds it from `--data`. `DARKORY_RUNNER_TMUX=off` (or `darkory runner --tmux off`) runs them as child processes, which cannot be joined. That server reads no tmux configuration (`-f /dev/null`): no status bar, 10000 lines of scrollback, `TERM=screen-256color`, none of the person's key tables or plugins.

**What a session runs with.** Its environment is the Runner's making, not the server's: `PATH` (the Runner's darkory first), `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, the proxy variables, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `DARKORY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` and, when set, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` from the server's, plus whatever the server's `DARKORY_RUNNER_ENV` names (comma-separated: where the secrets an agent needs go, since agent settings are every Member's to read), then `DARKORY_URL`, `DARKORY_TOKEN`, `DARKORY_SESSION` and the agent's `env`. A `serve` started inside Claude Code or a tmux session therefore hands its sessions no `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, `TMUX` or `TMUX_PANE`. Claude Code runs with **the person's own Claude Code configuration**: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` (or their `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), their sign-in from the Keychain or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, their trust decisions, and **their hooks, plugins, status line, `CLAUDE.md`, skills, agents, commands, MCP servers and permission rules, by their choice**: a status line can print their account and usage into the session's log, which is Evidence the Organisation reads, and a hook can start Claude sessions of its own (the check by hand in agents-plan.md's "Smoke run" saw a plugin's review session start on the builder's commit). The Runner writes none of it. A Workspace the person has opened in Claude Code is trusted already, and Claude Code keys the trust on the repository, so each Task's worktree is too; their `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, set once they accepted Bypass Permissions mode, covers `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Transcripts go to `~/.claude/projects/<the worktree's slug>/`.

A repository never opened in Claude Code makes it ask on a terminal, before any model turn, "Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust?" and, for a person who never accepted it, the Bypass Permissions mode warning. The Runner answers these only as a fallback, and narrowly, since anything the agent prints could imitate a dialog: in a Claude Code session in tmux, before the agent's model has answered at all (its transcript absent or with no assistant message), one dialog per session, and only when the visible screen is exactly that dialog of Claude Code 2.1.289 (the session's own folder in it, nothing under its "Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel"): Down and Enter, the only keys it ever presses into a session, and a Note "The runner accepted Claude Code's first-run prompt: …". Claude Code saves the answer in the person's own files, as if they had given it. A dialog it may not answer (after the first turn, or a second in the session, such as the bypass warning after the trust dialog for a person who never accepted it) gets no key: the session shows `waiting` and a Note says a person can answer it with `darkory join <KEY>`; unanswered, the Claim lapses on the usual rule.

The session's log, attached as Evidence when it ends, is the pane's output as the agent's terminal received it (`tmux pipe-pane`), nothing added or redacted, the person's status line included when they have one.

`tools/fakeagent` stands in for Claude Code: set an agent's command to it (`darkory agent set builder --command <path>/fakeagent --arg=--prompt-file --arg={prompt_file} --arg=--progress --arg=/tmp/p/{session_id}.jsonl --arg=--mcp-config --arg={mcp_config} --progress-file /tmp/p/{session_id}.jsonl --env FAKEAGENT_SCENARIO=handover`). It reads the prompt, writes its progress as a transcript, notes, commits in the first Workspace, attaches a test log, then per `FAKEAGENT_SCENARIO`: `complete` (default; a Break down first files `FAKEAGENT_BREAKDOWN`, `skill:title;…`, naming `FAKEAGENT_WORKSPACES`), `handover`, `question`, `silent`, `hang`, `busy` or `crash`. `FAKEAGENT_FILE` names the file it commits, so two Tasks can conflict. `FAKEAGENT_PROMPT` makes it draw Claude Code 2.1.289's folder-trust dialog and Bypass Permissions mode warning first and wait for Down, Enter: `claude` (as Claude Code does, unless the person's `~/.claude.json` or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trusts the folder or its repository and their settings accepted the skip), `trust`, or `again` (the trust dialog twice); `late` draws the trust dialog after its first turn instead, saying "the dialog was answered" should a Down reach it; the Runner treats it as Claude Code when it is started through a script named `claude`.

`DARKORY_RUNNER_TIMINGS` shortens the Runner's clocks for tests, as `name=duration` pairs: `wait` (next's wait, 30s), `timeout` (the Claims' heartbeat timeout, 5m), `tick` (progress read and Heartbeat, 30s), `stale` (no Heartbeat after, 2m), `nudge` (between nudges and before the release, 2m), `exit` (after /exit, 30s), `poll` (merged pull requests, 1m), `retry` (after a failure, 5s). The e2e tests use `wait=1s,timeout=10s,tick=200ms,stale=2s,nudge=700ms,exit=3s,poll=1s,retry=300ms`.

What the tests hold:

- `internal/runner` unit tests: the command template (placeholders, Claude Code's defaults and first message, the permission skip, a misspelt placeholder), shell quoting through a real `sh`; the transcript's project slug and real path, the turn-ended reading of Claude Code 2.1's records and of `TURN_ENDED`, a transcript longer than the tail read; the prompt (golden files in `testdata/`, `go test ./internal/runner -run TestBuildPrompt -update` rewrites them), escapes and quoted record text included; the checkout planner; `Prepare` against real git (the Break down making `feature/<KEY>`, a later session reusing the worktree or the branch, removal keeping the branch and a dirty worktree, a person's branch refused, a quick Feature from main); every merge path (merge-tree into a branch checked out nowhere, two parents, nothing touched; again is a no-op; a conflict moves nothing; into the checked-out main, clean, and its conflict aborted; uncommitted changes refusing it); the child and tmux hosts (environment from a 0600 file, typed lines, the pane's log, exit status, kill); the pane tail with escapes taken out. After the smoke run: a session's environment (`TestBaseEnv`, `DARKORY_RUNNER_ENV`; `TestChildHostEnvironment`, `TestTmuxHostEnvironment` on a tmux server started with `CLAUDECODE` in its own environment); the tmux server reading no configuration from a `HOME` whose `.tmux.conf` sets options (`TestTmuxHostReadsNoConfiguration`); and the first-run dialogs found exactly on the smoke's capture and a fresh directory's, and not for another folder, with Claude Code's prompt under them, with the choice moved, in the older wording or as words in a line (`TestFindFirstRunPrompt`); a transcript's first assistant message (`TestHasAssistantMessage`).
- `internal/runner` in-process tests (`runner_test.go`, both engines, the test binary standing in for darkory and the fake agent built once): a Feature from filing to Ship (the planner's Break down, the builder's Handover, the reviewer's Complete, the merge into `feature/WEB-1` and Ship into main's checkout, two session logs, worktrees gone); a silent session nudged twice, released three times and escalated to the owner (three `session-WEB-3-builder-<HHMMSS>.log`); a session in tmux on the Runner's own server, gone once its Claim ends, its log the Evidence byte for byte; a `claude` script running the fake agent with `FAKEAGENT_PROMPT=claude`, which asks as Claude Code does unless the person's configuration has answered, completing with no prompt in a worktree of a repository a test `HOME`'s `.claude.json` trusts, that file and their settings left byte for byte (`TestRunnerUsesThePersonsClaudeCodeConfiguration`, both engines), and in tmux the trust dialog accepted with a Note, then in the next session a second dialog left to a person, the session `waiting` with its Note (`TestRunnerAnswersOneFirstRunPrompt`), and the exact dialog printed after the agent's first turn getting no key at all (`TestRunnerNeverAnswersAfterTheFirstTurn`); the reviewer's session starting within 2 s of the builder's end with a 5 s tick (`TestRunnerStartsTheNextSessionOnceTheEarlierEnds`); a hanging agent's session going running then stalled, a silent one's waiting (`TestRunnerSessionStates`); the terminal through `/v1/runner/sessions/{task}/terminal` (an admin's keys reach the agent and a Note says they joined; a non-admin's never do, even asking `?readonly=0`, nor an admin's asking `?readonly=1`; watching writes no Note, and a watcher's 40 columns leave the agent's window at the admin's 100). `pr_test.go` (SQLite, as are the two tmux tests): a `pull_request` Workspace with `gh` stubbed — a merged pull request carrying the Task's key completes its review as an agent that may review, with a Note; one without a key is ignored; the runner merges nothing itself; Ship opens the Feature branch's pull request.
- `internal/mcp` `TestNoHeartbeatsLeavesTheClaimToTheRunner`; `cmd/darkory` `TestJoinNeedsASession`, `TestRunnerNeedsTokens`; `internal/config` the `--runner` setting.
- `e2e/runner_test.go` (`make e2e`, `make e2e-pg`): darkory init's roster in a fresh repository, every agent on the fake agent, serve's Runner with the timings above: `TestRunnerWorksAFeature` (scenarios 2, 3, 4, 11: two Workspaces on each Task, two builders, merges in both repositories noted on the Tasks, Ship), `TestRunnerEndsSessionsWithoutADecision` (5, 6 with the hung session `stalled` through `/v1`, 7), `TestRunnerQuickAndShipWhenDone` (4), `TestRunnerMergeConflict` (9), `TestRunnerAlone` (12: `darkory runner` beside `serve --runner=off`), `TestRunnerInTmux` (skipped without tmux: `dk-MAIN-2` on the Runner's tmux server, stopped by an admin through `/v1`). The harness starts every other test's server with `--runner=off`.

## The Postgres the tests need

Postgres 14 or newer, and a role that may create databases. The URL names any database the role can connect to (`postgres` is fine); tests never write to it. Each test creates its own database, `dk_test_<random>`, from `template0`, and drops it `WITH (FORCE)` when the test ends, so packages can run in parallel against one server.

A throwaway local server on the port the Makefile expects:

```sh
initdb -D /tmp/dk-pg -U dk --auth=trust
pg_ctl -D /tmp/dk-pg -o "-p 54329" -l /tmp/dk-pg.log start
```

or with Docker:

```sh
docker run -d --name dk-pg -p 54329:5432 -e POSTGRES_USER=dk -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust postgres:14
```

If a test run is killed before its cleanup, drop what it left behind:

```sh
psql "$DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -Atc "SELECT 'DROP DATABASE \"' || datname || '\" WITH (FORCE);' FROM pg_database WHERE datname LIKE 'dk_test_%'" | psql "$DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL"
```

## Writing a test that runs on both

Use `internal/store/storetest`. `Each` runs the body once per engine as subtests named `sqlite` and `postgres`, each with a fresh, migrated database:

```go
func TestSomething(t *testing.T) {
	storetest.Each(t, func(t *testing.T, s *store.Store) {
		org := storetest.Organisation(t, s)
		err := s.Write(t.Context(), org, func(tx store.Tx, seq int64) error {
			// …
		})
		// …
	})
}
```

- `storetest.Open(t, engine)` and `storetest.OpenUnmigrated(t, engine)` give one database on a named engine.
- `storetest.DSN(t, engine)` gives an empty database's DSN, for tests that open several Stores on one database.
- A Postgres-only test asks for `store.Postgres` directly; it skips when the URL is unset.

Write queries once, with `$1, $2…` placeholders; both drivers accept them, repeated and in any order.

## What guards what

- `internal/store`: `Write` numbers Activity without gaps in commit order under 50 concurrent writers, with no "database is locked" on SQLite; the migration runner, its SQLite backup and its refusal of a newer database; `TestSchemaIsTheSameOnBothEngines` compares tables, columns, nullability, primary keys, indexes and foreign keys after migrating each engine (it skips without Postgres, having nothing to compare with); `TestEveryTableCarriesOrgID`.
- `internal/server/gen`: `TestSpecKeepsTheConventions` validates `api/openapi.yaml` and checks every operation for `Idempotency-Key` on writes, the credential requirement, and the `Error` default response.
- `internal/store` also: `WriteBatch` takes the counter first and a failed guard rolls everything back; `TestWriteBatchIsOneRoundTripOnPostgres` counts the round trips on the wire (`storetest.Wire`).
- `internal/core`, on both engines with a fake clock (`clock.Fake`): every branch of the Takeable rule and its negative (`rule_test.go`); lapses at expiry, a late Heartbeat refused, the lapse recorded once by whoever meets it first, Session binding, revocation and close ending Claims, idempotent claims (`claim_test.go`); admin operations, the admin mark, Reporting-line cycles, filing (`admin_test.go`). The race suite (`race_test.go`): 50 claims of one Task give one winner and 49 `already_claimed`; 20 `next` callers over 10 Tasks claim each once and leave nothing takeable; a late Heartbeat racing a claimer and the sweeper records one lapse; a reader following `after` under concurrent writers sees every Activity number in order; concurrent retries under one Idempotency-Key make one write. `TestHotPathWritesAreOneRoundTripOnPostgres` checks claim, `next`'s claim, heartbeat, release and complete each send one batch in one round trip. Run the race suite repeatedly with `go test -race -count=5 -run Race ./internal/core/`.
- `internal/core`, Phase 2: Handover and no self-review, the holder's Notes and Observations, take-back up the Reporting line, the owner's Task drop (`flow_test.go`); Blocking across Features, cycles, the authority to block, questions and Escalations (`blocking_test.go`); Rank, ship, drop and its cascade, ownership, the owner's fallback for the Break down and the Retrospective, a Retrospective sorting by its ended Feature's Rank (`features_test.go`); proposals, publishing, the stale base, the author's refusal, Observations reviewed, a Feature filed from a Retrospective (`retro_test.go`); every Activity kind written is listed (`kinds_test.go`). Races: two opposite block edges and a triangle never both close (`TestRaceOppositeBlockEdges`, run it with `-count=20`); ship against filing a Task (`TestRaceShipAgainstFilingATask`). The round-trip test also covers handover, note, observe and a publishing complete.
- `internal/blob`: the disk store's put, get and delete; keys that would leave the store are refused; a short, long or cancelled put leaves no file.
- `internal/server`: health with its sign-in modes, JSON 404s under `/v1`, and the web app at `/`; through the generated Go client on both engines: no credential is 401 even from 127.0.0.1, a token without a Session is `session_required`, the claim path from filing a Feature to completing its Break down, idempotency keys, a login link signing a browser in, the Activity stream resuming with `Last-Event-ID`, and its first bytes (`: connected`) arriving at once, before any event or keep-alive. `security_test.go`: a cookie write from another origin, a sibling port or with no Origin or Referer is 403 while one from the Install's own origin passes and bearer writes need no Origin; JSON bodies need `application/json`; the Activity stream ends without sending more once its token is revoked or its Session closed. `flow_test.go`: health's sign-in modes and update notice; Activity read backwards and the stream from now; the Activity enums match the core; Evidence on both engines (the holder and Team rules, the size limit, path filenames, retries, nosniff attachments). `mvp_test.go`: the MVP flow through the generated client on both engines, from a human filing a Feature to a published Skill version and a later Claim under it. In `internal/core`, `TestRevocationStopsLongRequestsAndClaims` covers a waiting `next` and a claim from an ended Session.
- `cmd/darkory`: `init` runs once and prints a token and a login link; `serve` prints a startup link and opens it unless told not to, and with `--no-login-link` issues none. `migrate --dry-run` lists and applies nothing, `migrate` applies, both and `serve` refuse a newer database, and `serve` on Postgres refuses pending migrations without `--migrate`.
- `internal/wake` (Postgres): a Signal in one process wakes that Organisation's waiters in another and no others; an idle LISTEN connection survives its pings; killing it (`pg_terminate_backend`) wakes every waiter once it is back, and later Signals arrive again; a LISTEN that never hears its own probe is reported; bursts coalesce and a failed NOTIFY is resent. `TestWritesOnOneProcessWakeWaitersOnAnother` runs two Stores and two HTTP servers on one database: a waiting `next` and an Activity stream on A answer within 1 s of a write on B, before and after both LISTEN connections are killed.
- `internal/blob`, with `DARKORY_TEST_S3=1` and Docker: put, get and delete against MinIO; a missing key is `ErrNotFound`; a reader that fails, ends early or is cancelled leaves nothing; 50 MiB streams with the heap growing by kilobytes; a wrong secret fails without showing it; Evidence attached through `/v1` to an Install set to S3 lands in the bucket under its prefix and downloads back.
- `internal/auth`: the rate limiter's burst and refill; ten times its cap of new keys keeps it at the cap with the most recent kept and none refused; a limited key that keeps trying is never evicted into a fresh bucket.
- `internal/mail`: STARTTLS with AUTH PLAIN, implicit TLS, refusing plain text unless `tls=none`, an untrusted certificate, a silent server, and header injection, all against an in-process SMTP server. `internal/server/signin_test.go`: an emailed link signs a browser in once and expires at 15 minutes; unknown addresses send nothing; the reply comes before the send; per-Member and per-client limits, a Member asked for from 20 clients held to their limit, 10,000 made-up addresses from as many /64s creating no Member key and taking no token from the cap, an IPv6 client limited by its /64, and the cap on emails sent (202, nothing issued, one warning a minute, refilled over the hour); no email without a mailer or a public URL; `X-Forwarded-For` with `--proxy-hops`. With `DARKORY_TEST_SMTP=1` and Docker, the same round trip through Mailpit.
- `internal/cli`, against a real in-process server on both engines: the claim path from filing a Feature to completing a Task, with `--json` decoding as the /v1 types; exit statuses 1–4 and how errors print; refusing Session-bound work without `DARKORY_SESSION`; a lost reply retried once under the same Idempotency-Key writing once (`dropReply`); `prime` evaluated by `sh`; `heartbeat run` keeping a 2 s Claim alive and the Claim lapsing once it stops, and `--background` with the test binary standing in for darkory (`TestMain`); `activity --follow`; the admin commands; `health` and `login --email` with a fake mail sender, one email for a Member's address and the same reply for any other; terminal controls and bidi overrides in what other Members wrote escaped in text output and `--json` round-tripping them exactly (`escape_test.go`). Phase 2 commands are also checked against a recording fake for method, path, query, body and headers; `TestPhase2Flow` runs them against the real server on both engines, from Notes, Evidence and a blocking question through Handover, take-back, ship, a proposal read with `proposal show` and published by review, to dropping a Feature. `activity --follow` starts from now unless `--all`. `internal/cli/remote`: which failed requests are sent again, keys on writes only, and `Clean`, `CleanLine` and `CleanJSON`.
- `internal/mcp`, through the SDK's in-memory transport against a real server: the tools, prompt, resource and instructions; `next`, `claim` and `complete` with structured output, refusals as tool errors carrying the code; Heartbeats keeping a 2 s Claim alive; a Claim lapsing under a fake server clock reported once in the next tool result; a Retrospective with `observations`, `propose_skill_version` and `show_proposal`, and `activity` paging backwards; tool text escaped while structured content stays exact; `attach_evidence` refusing a path outside the evidence root, `..`, a symlink out, hidden names, devices, pipes, directories and oversized files (`evidence_test.go`).
- Found end to end and held by tests in their packages: `internal/cli` `TestHeartbeatRunFindsALaterClaimInTime` (a background heartbeat started before the Claim on a short token default keeps it); `internal/core` `TestRaceIdempotentRetriesOfHeldWrites` (concurrent retries of release, handover and complete under one key all get the first response), `TestClaimNeverStartsBeforeThePreviousClaimEnded` (a claim timed before the previous Claim's end is refused and retried, so Claim intervals never overlap) and `TestUnblockingAQuestionOnAnEndedFeature` (the last edge of an open question on an ended Feature stays); `internal/config` `serve --no-update-check`.
- `e2e/` (`DARKORY_E2E=1`): `TestMVPFlow`, the six steps of the map's MVP flow with a human owner and six agents, each with its own token and Session — the Break down through `darkory mcp`, Handover through qa-acme, ui-review and security-review, the builder refused the qa stage, a blocking question answered by the owner while qa keeps its Claim, a test report and a PNG screenshot, ship refused while Tasks are open, the Retrospective proposing qa-acme v2 that its author cannot publish and a reviewer from another Team does, a Feature filed from it and a later Claim under version 2 with its model label. `TestLapseAndRecovery`: `heartbeat run --background` started before `next` keeps a Claim on the token's 5 s default; killed with SIGKILL, the Claim lapses, another Session of the Member and then another Member claim, the dead Session's late `heartbeat` exits 3 `lapsed`, and Activity records one lapse. `TestMCPKeepsItsClaimsAlive`: the same for `darkory mcp`. `TestTwoServersOnePostgres`: a `next` waiting on one server answers within a second of a Task filed on another, and `activity --follow` on the first prints the second's writes, gapless. `TestSoak`: 40 Sessions of 4 agents, two human filers and a stream reader per server, for `DARKORY_E2E_SOAK`, then the invariants (Claims on a Task never overlap, no Member holds a Task under two Skills, Activity gapless and every stream saw it all in order, every Task's state agrees with its Claims, one `task.lapsed` per lapsed Claim, Idempotency-Key retries — sequential and concurrent — answer alike and file nothing twice, no 5xx, no busy database in any reply or server log); it logs requests a second and p50/p99 for claim and next. Every server and MCP log is checked for `level=ERROR`, a locked database, a data race or a panic. `TestImportsNothingInternal` holds the package, and the bots it runs (`tools/bots`), to the binary's surfaces. `TestBots` and `TestBotsAccounting`: the bots of each preset at work, with the scenarios and the trail described under [Bots](#bots).
- Security review fixes (`docs/build/security-review.md`), each with a regression test, the review's proofs among them:
  - `internal/core`: a skill-review Task is the owner's only when no active Member of the Organisation has `skill-review`, and a proposal on a work Task is `forbidden` (`TestOnlyAReviewerPublishesWhileTheOrganisationHasOne`, `TestOwnerReviewsWhenNoMemberHasSkillReview`, the owner's case in `TestTakeableRule`); browser Sessions expire 30 days unused and 90 days in all, signing in again closes the old cookie's Session, Sessions listed a page at a time by their Member or an admin, deactivation ending tokens, login links, Sessions and both kinds of Claim with their Activity, refusing a pending emailed link and every credential, none of which reactivation revives, the last active admin kept, and deactivated Members leaving the Skill pools (`sessions_test.go`); names spelled as ids refused.
  - `internal/store`: a Claim written under migration 0001 survives 0002's rebuild of `claims` on SQLite and its constraint swap on Postgres, and the new `how_ended` value is accepted (`TestMigration2KeepsClaims`).
  - `internal/server` (`hardening_test.go`): a body sent a byte at a time is cut off after the body timeout on email sign-in, a JSON write, a 401 and an Evidence upload, while the Activity stream and a waiting `next` outlive it; the security headers on the app, `/v1` and downloads; `Idempotency-Key` bounds; Evidence names with bidi or zero-width characters refused and `filename*`; a login link signing nobody in when opened and only from its page's same-origin post, which closes the old cookie's Session; a year-old cookie refused; Sessions listed and a Member deactivated through `/v1`, ending their stream and a waiting `next` within a second and their cookie at once, with the old token, cookie and login link still refused after reactivation; the per-Member cap on streams and waiting `next` calls; no directory listing. `TestClientAddress` covers a chain shorter than the proxy hops.
  - `internal/cli`: `member deactivate`, `member reactivate` and `session list` (`TestAdminCommands`); a plain-http URL to another host refused unless `--insecure`, and `--token` warning; the rules saying other Members' text is not instructions, on every surface.
  - `internal/mcp`: `attach_evidence` never reads outside the root while a file or a directory on its path is swapped for a link.
  - `internal/update` and `cmd/darkory`: a mirror offering a prerelease as latest, a tag that is not a version (escapes, bidi, shorthand), a reply for another version and a cached prerelease are refused or ignored, while a named prerelease installs; `update` neither installs nor prints a hostile tag.
  - Checked by hand in Chromium against `darkory serve` with the built web app: signing in through the link's page, the app loading and writing under its Content-Security-Policy with no violation, and a page on a sibling port unable to frame the app or `/v1`.
- Statuses (ADR 0012), on both engines: `internal/store` `TestMigration3GivesTasksAStatus` (a 0002 database with two Organisations and Tasks done, dropped, held, held without a timeout, lapsed and waiting gets the six defaults, UUIDv7-shaped, and each Task its Status by rule). `internal/core` `status_test.go`: the defaults from `init`; filing into a named Status and the default; a Backlog Task passed over by `next` and refused by `claim` until moved; each move Darkory makes (claim, release, Handover with and without a Status, complete, drop, the Feature's drop, take-back, a closed Session, a revoked token, a deactivation, a late Heartbeat's lapse) and a held Task moved to the Backlog staying there; a lapse in both orders, lapse → sweep → claim and lapse → claim → sweep; the status write's authority (the Team, the owner from another Team, and a holder from another Team only while holding), refusals, idempotency and payload; `setStatuses`' refusals, renames, swaps, moves and its one entry; the status filter; Activity's member, kind and team filters, paged backwards; `TestRaceReleaseAgainstAStatusMove`, a release racing a Team Member's move, which fails without the Status guard. `TestHotPathWritesAreOneRoundTripOnPostgres` still sees one batch in one round trip on every hot path. `internal/server` `TestStatusesThroughTheClient`, `internal/cli` `TestStatusCommands` and the new rows of `TestPhase2CommandsFormTheirRequests`, `internal/mcp` `TestStatusTools`. The soak checks every Task's Status against its state and its last Claim.
- `web/src/**/*.test.ts(x)`: the web app against a stubbed `fetch` (`src/test/api.ts`) and a fake `EventSource` (`src/test/eventSource.ts`): the signed-out page on 401, the board in Rank order, refusals shown with their code, admin hidden from non-admins, a token's secret shown once, and Activity events refetching open views; Phase 4a: Task counts from the Feature, ranking by drag, open blockers, the Skill proposal and its stale base, the email form only with `email_link`, the update notice and its dismissal, revoking one's own token and closing a Session, Activity read backwards with `before`, its kinds in words, and the history re-read when the stream skips ahead.
- `web/e2e/flow.spec.ts` (`npm run e2e`): Chromium against the real binary on a fresh SQLite record: no cookie shows the signed-out page; the startup link signs in; the admin creates a Team, an agent Member, grants Skills and issues a token shown once; a filed Feature shows its Break down; the agent's claim through `/v1` appears without a reload; a refused ship shows `tasks_open`; the human claims, notes, attaches a PNG (downloaded back as an attachment) and completes; Features are ranked by dragging and stay ranked after a reload; shipping files the Retrospective; a proposal written on it in the browser and reviewed by the agent shows published without a reload; Activity reads in words; the board at 390 px has no sideways scroll. Screenshots land in `web/e2e/screenshots/`.
- Agents R0 (`docs/build/agents-plan.md`), on both engines: `internal/store` `TestMigration4AddsWorkspacesAndAgents` (a 0003 database upgraded, the defaults and the new tables' checks). `internal/core` `agents_test.go`: Workspaces added, changed and removed by admins, names unique ignoring case, a named Workspace never removed and a Team's default cleared with it (`TestWorkspaces`); a Task naming the Workspaces it is filed with in order, else its Team's default, `[]` naming none (`TestTaskWorkspaces`); a quick Feature's one Task, its refusals, its review shipping it in the same write and no Retrospective (`TestQuickFeature`); ship-when-done from the Feature or the Team's default, the trail completed → shipped → Retrospective filed, nothing on a drop or on an ended Feature (`TestShipWhenDone`, `TestShipWhenDoneOnAnEndedFeature`); agent settings merged over the defaults with their Activity (`TestAgentSettings`); `InitWith`'s roster (`TestInitSeedsTheRoster`); Notes on a Task nobody holds by its owner or Team, the holder alone on a held one (`TestNotesOnATaskNobodyHolds`). `TestHotPathWritesAreOneRoundTripOnPostgres` also measures a complete that ships its Feature and files the Retrospective. `internal/server` `agents_test.go`: the operations through the client, and the Runner's endpoints with a fake Runner — the list's `runner: false`, `no_runner` on nudge, stop and the terminal, a non-admin joining read-only whatever they ask, and a cookie upgrade refused unless it comes from the Install's own pages. `internal/cli` `TestAgentCommands`, `internal/mcp` `TestWorkspaceTools`, `internal/gitinfo` `TestFind`, `cmd/darkory` `TestInitSeedsTheRosterInAGitRepository` and `TestInitOutsideAGitRepository`. `e2e/` `TestInitSeedsTheRoster`: `darkory init` without `--no-agents` in a fresh git repository, the roster, Team MAIN, the Workspace and the four token files, each token working; every other e2e test runs `init --no-agents`, but `TestBots`, which runs on a seeded Install.
